title: Passing a uniform torsion bound to an affine limit
statement:
Let $X=\varprojlim_i X_i$ be a filtered inverse limit of
quasi-compact
quasi-separated schemes with affine transition maps.
If $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(X_i)\leq c$ for every $i$,
then $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(X)\leq c$, with bounds as in
[def-sc-etale-torsion-cd].

proof.text:
First check that $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-cone-affine-projections-opens], each projection $p_i:X\to X_i$ is affine. Fix a stage and a finite affine open cover of $X_i$. Its inverse images are affine and cover $X$, proving quasi-compactness. Each intersection of two members of the stage cover is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion], hence has a finite affine open cover. Pulling this latter cover back along the affine projection gives a finite affine cover of the corresponding intersection in $X$. The converse in that criterion proves quasi-separatedness of $X$.

Write $p_i^*$ for the abelian-sheaf inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], with direct image as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For $j\geq i$, the counit of $p_{ji}^*\dashv p_{ji*}$ applied to $F_j=p_{j*}F$, together with $p_{ji*}F_j=F_i$, gives the stated transition. Its compatibility under composition follows by adjunction from the identity of the composite direct-image functors, which is the associative fibre-product identity on sections. The counits to $F$ form a compatible cocone.

Let $p_i:X\to X_i$, and first let $F$ be killed by a fixed
integer $n>0$. Set $F_i=p_{i*}F$; for $j\geq i$
the adjunction maps give transition arrows
$p_{ji}^*F_i\to F_j$, and hence arrows
$p_i^*F_i\to p_j^*F_j$ on $X$.
The canonical map $\varinjlim_i p_i^*F_i\to F$ is an
isomorphism. To verify it, use quasi-compact etale objects
of finite presentation: every such object and every morphism
between two of them descends to a stage of the inverse system.
A section of $F$ on a descended object is, by definition,
a section of $p_{i*}F$ on that object at stage $i$, proving
surjectivity locally. If two representatives agree after
pullback, their equality is witnessed on a finite covering family of etale maps;
the covering and the finitely many maps in it descend to a
later stage. This proves injectivity after sheafification.
The object, morphism, relation and covering descent used here are the clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-finite-data-descent], rather than an appeal to the proof of continuity.
More explicitly, affine etale objects cover every etale object. Since $X$ is quasi-separated, an affine etale object is of finite presentation over $X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), so the object descent theorem applies to this basis. Inverse-image sheafification means that locally each representative in $p_i^*F_i$ is given by an etale object $V_i$ over $X_i$, a map into its base change to $X$, and a section of $F_i(V_i)=F((V_i)_X)$. Restrict to affine neighbourhoods in these objects; on a quasi-compact basis object the necessary local covers have finite affine refinements by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-qcqs-cofinal-finite-coverings]. The finitely many objects and maps then descend by finite-data descent. For injectivity it suffices to consider a representative whose image in $F$ is zero. After descending its representing map to stage $j$, its restriction becomes a section of $F_j(U_j)=F((U_j)_X)$ on a descended object. This section is zero by the assumed equality in $F$, and its image in $p_j^*F_j$ is therefore zero. A finite cover handles representatives given only locally. Applying this to the difference of two representatives proves injectivity. No arbitrary section of $F$ is asserted to descend as a sheaf on a stage.

proof.text:
The direct-image sheaf $F_i=p_{i*}F$ is killed by $n$: on an etale object $U_i$ its sections are $F(U_i\times_{X_i}X)$, so multiplication by $n$ is zero. Its inverse images $p_{ji}^*F_i$ are also killed by $n$, hence torsion. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-continuity] to $F_i$. The uniform bound at every later stage gives
$$H^q(X,p_i^*F_i)=\varinjlim_{j\geq i}H^q(X_j,p_{ji}^*F_i)=0\quad(q>c).$$

source.place: ## Proof, paragraph 2 (expanded using the cited node statements)

proof.text: For each fixed exponent $n$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-filtered-colimit] to the isomorphism from Step 1. Since every term $H^q(X,p_i^*F_i)$ vanishes for $q>c$ by Step 2, this gives $H^q(X,F)=0$ for $q>c$. For an arbitrary torsion sheaf $F$, [lemma-weil-pbc-torsion-filtered-union] writes $F$ as the filtered colimit of the subsheaves $F[n]$. Apply the same fixed-exponent argument to each $F[n]$, then apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-filtered-colimit] once more to obtain $H^q(X,F)=0$ for $q>c$.
